proposals.before: 〈The gloss reads the character with the same sound as dao, 'way."
proposals.after: 〈The gloss reads the character with the same sound as dao, 'way.'〉
proposals.reason: Broken quotation marks and missing closing annotation bracket; the note only gives the pronunciation dao.

proposals.before: After Sun Hao shifted the capital he grew wary of Fan Shen's stature and issued an edict: "Fan's achievements and character alike command respect; I lean on him with reverence. He should be promoted to grand preceptor to satisfy public expectation."
proposals.after: After Sun Hao shifted the capital he grew wary of Fan Shen's stature and issued an edict: "Fan's achievements and character alike command respect; I lean on him with reverence. He should be raised to the highest ducal rank to satisfy public expectation."
proposals.reason: 上公 is the highest ducal rank (the Three Dukes), not specifically the office of grand preceptor (太師); the next sentence appoints him grand commandant.

proposals.before: Sun Deng's birth mother had been a woman of humble station. Lady Xu had raised him briefly in his childhood, but she was later cast aside for jealousy and sent to live in Wu, while Consort Lady Bu became Sun Quan's favorite.
proposals.after: Sun Deng's birth mother had been a woman of humble station. Lady Xu had had the grace of mothering him in his youth, but she was later cast aside for jealousy and sent to live in Wu, while Consort Lady Bu became Sun Quan's favorite.
proposals.reason: 少有母養之恩 means she mothered him when he was young, not that she raised him only briefly.

proposals.before: "In Wu," he answered."
proposals.after: "In Wu," he answered.
proposals.reason: Extraneous closing quotation mark after the narrative verb.

proposals.before: I know life and death are decreed and longevity is heaven's gift. The Zhou and Jin kings and Yan Hui were men of supreme intellect, yet they died young—how much more I, dull and obscure, who have already outlived my share, lived as your heir, and will depart with honors few could claim? What room is left for regret?
proposals.after: I know life and death are decreed and longevity is heaven's gift. Prince Jin of Zhou and Yan Hui were men of supreme intellect, yet they died young—how much more I, dull and obscure, who have already outlived my share, lived as your heir, and will depart with honors few could claim? What room is left for regret?
proposals.reason: 周晉 names Prince Jin of Zhou (太子晉), one person, not separate Zhou and Jin kings.

proposals.before: Your servant has heard that death and life have their allotment and length and brevity come from Heaven; the kings of Zhou and Jin and Yan Hui had talents of the highest wisdom, yet still met early death—how much more your servant, stupid and mean, his years having passed his allotted span, who in life was heir of the state and in death will enjoy glorious fortune—for your servant it is already much; what grief or resentment is there!
proposals.after: Your servant has heard that death and life have their allotment and length and brevity come from Heaven; Prince Jin of Zhou and Yan Hui had talents of the highest wisdom, yet still met early death—how much more your servant, stupid and mean, his years having passed his allotted span, who in life was heir of the state and in death will enjoy glorious fortune—for your servant it is already much; what grief or resentment is there!
proposals.reason: 周晉 is Prince Jin of Zhou, not 'kings of Zhou and Jin'.

proposals.before: Your servant has heard that in governing one listens to the people; statutes and ordinances shift with the times; truly one ought with generals, ministers, and great officials carefully choose what fits the times, broadly gather the multitude's proposals, widen punishments and lighten levies, evenly still labor and corvée, so as to comply with the people's hopes.
proposals.after: Your servant has heard that in governing one listens to the people; statutes and ordinances shift with the times; truly one ought with generals, ministers, and great officials carefully choose what fits the times, broadly gather the multitude's proposals, relax punishments and lighten levies, evenly still labor and corvée, so as to comply with the people's hopes.
proposals.reason: 寬刑 means to relax or ease punishments, not to widen them.

proposals.before: Sun Quan agreed. Sun Lü received the imperial baton, opened his own command, and governed half the province.
proposals.after: Sun Quan agreed. Sun Lu received the imperial baton, opened his own command, and governed half the province.
proposals.reason: 孫慮 is elsewhere rendered Sun Lu; Sun Lü is an inconsistent transliteration in this unit.

proposals.before: Sun Lü's bearing is noble and his military talent proven—he can help secure the great work. So I invest him as a supreme general, grant him extraordinary honor, put troops at his disposal, and charge him with a frontier command.
proposals.after: Sun Lu's bearing is noble and his military talent proven—he can help secure the great work. So I invest him as a supreme general, grant him extraordinary honor, put troops at his disposal, and charge him with a frontier command.
proposals.reason: Same person 慮 is Sun Lu elsewhere in the chunk.

proposals.before: Sun He, courtesy name Zixiao, was Lu's younger brother.
proposals.after: Sun He, courtesy name Zixiao, was Sun Lü's younger brother.
proposals.reason: Literal English drops the surname already supplied in the idiomatic line and in the Chinese 慮 as Sun Lü.

proposals.before: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Yuanji, was the son of Dun.
proposals.after: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Yuanji, was the son of Zhang Dun.
proposals.reason: Literal English leaves the father as bare Dun although the idiomatic rendering identifies Zhang Dun.

proposals.before: When Area Commander Liu Bao and palace attendant Ding Yan denounced each other, Sun He told Ding Yan, "How few men truly hold office! To nurse grudges and plot mutual ruin can only bring ruin on us all."
proposals.after: When Area Commander Liu Bao and the heir's cadet Ding Yan denounced each other, Sun He told Ding Yan, "How few men truly hold office! To nurse grudges and plot mutual ruin can only bring ruin on us all."
proposals.reason: 庶子 here is a Crown Prince household office, not a generic palace attendant.

proposals.before: Sun Quan once lay ill with a sleeping sickness; He performed sacrifice and prayer in the temple; He's consort's paternal uncle Zhang Xiu dwelt near the temple and invited He to pass his dwelling.
proposals.after: Sun Quan once lay ill; He performed sacrifice and prayer in the temple; He's consort's paternal uncle Zhang Xiu dwelt near the temple and invited He to pass his dwelling.
proposals.reason: 寢疾 means to take to one's sickbed, not a diagnosis of sleeping sickness.

proposals.before: she also said that when Lady Wang saw the sovereign lying ill with a sleeping sickness, she had a joyful expression.
proposals.after: she also said that when Lady Wang saw the sovereign lying ill, she had a joyful expression.
proposals.reason: Same 寢疾 error: illness in bed, not sleeping sickness.

proposals.before: Pei Songzhi comments: Yuan Shao and Liu Biao genuinely preferred their younger sons—unlike Sun Quan, who had already named an heir yet doted on Sun Ba, inviting ruin at home. Beside them Sun Quan looks far more blind.
proposals.after: Pei Songzhi comments: Yuan Shao and Liu Biao held Shang and Cong worthy and originally meant to pass the succession to them—unlike Sun Quan, who had already named an heir yet doted on Sun Ba, inviting ruin at home. Beside Yuan and Liu, Sun Quan looks far more blind.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the named sons 尚 and 琮 and the short names 袁、劉.

proposals.before: When Sun Quan meant to depose Sun He for Sun Liang, colonels Chen Zheng and Chen Xiang cited Duke Xian of Jin, who killed Crown Prince Sheng to install Xi Qi and threw the state into chaos; Zhu Ju and Qu Huang still would not let the matter drop.
proposals.after: When Sun Quan meant to depose Sun He for Sun Liang, colonels Chen Zheng and Chen Xiang cited Duke Xian of Jin, who killed Shen Sheng to install Xi Qi and threw the state into chaos; Zhu Ju and Qu Huang still would not let the matter drop.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English reduces 申生 to Crown Prince Sheng, dropping the given name Shen preserved in the Chinese and the literal rendering.

proposals.before: Your servant wishes Your Majesty slightly to let fall sagely consideration; though your aged servant die, it is still as the years of his life."
proposals.after: Your servant wishes Your Majesty slightly to let fall sagely consideration; though your aged servant die, it would still count as years of life."
proposals.reason: The literal closing 猶生之年 is calqued into unintelligible English; the Chinese means dying would still be as good as living.

proposals.before: The consort sent Yellow Gate Attendant Chen Qian to Jiankang to submit a memorial to the inner palace and also to convey inquiries to Zhuge Ke.
proposals.after: The consort sent Yellow Gate Attendant Chen Qian to Jianye to submit a memorial to the inner palace and also to convey inquiries to Zhuge Ke.
proposals.reason: 建業 is Jianye, the Wu capital's contemporary name; Jiankang is the later name and is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: In the first month of the following year, again he divided nine counties of Wu commandery and Danyang to make Wu commandery of Xing, administering Wucheng, and established a grand administrator, with seasonal sacrifice in four seasons.
proposals.after: In the first month of the following year, again he divided nine counties of Wu commandery and Danyang to make Wu Xing commandery, with its seat at Wucheng, and established a grand administrator, with seasonal sacrifice in the four seasons.
proposals.reason: 吳興郡 is Wu Xing commandery, not 'Wu commandery of Xing'.

proposals.before: Before reaching thirty li they halted, chose an auspicious day, but only sent envoys with Qian's order to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.
proposals.after: Before reaching thirty li they halted, chose an auspicious day, and Dan sent envoys with Qian's order to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.
proposals.reason: 但遣使 uses the personal name 但 (Shi Dan), not the adverb 'but only'.

proposals.before: Shi Dan's men fought stripped of armor, hair streaming loose.
proposals.after: Shi Dan's soldiers were naked, without armor; when they faced the battle line they all scattered.
proposals.reason: 披散 here means the troops broke and scattered, not that they wore their hair loose.

proposals.before: But Dan's soldiers were naked without armor; facing battle they all let their hair hang loose.
proposals.after: Dan's soldiers were naked without armor; facing battle they all scattered.
proposals.reason: Initial 但 is the name Dan; 披散 means they dispersed, not loosened hair.

proposals.before: You should look upward to Taibo's yielding spirit, inward to the restraint of Han's virtuous princes, and downward to the warning of pride and license.
proposals.after: You should look upward to Taibo's yielding to his father's will, in the middle recall the reverent restraint of Prince Xian of Hejian and Prince Qiang of the Eastern Sea, and downward restrain arrogance, license, waste, and disorder as a warning.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the two named Han princes 河間獻王 and 東海王彊 and the 'yield to father' sense of 順父, collapsing them into an unnamed 'Han's virtuous princes'.

proposals.before: Zhuge Ke sent him a written remonstrance: "The Son of Heaven shares rank with Heaven; the empire is his household, and every subject is his servant.
proposals.after: Zhuge Ke sent him a written remonstrance: "The honor of emperors and kings shares rank with Heaven; therefore they treat the realm as a household, and even fathers and elder brothers among the subjects are subjects and servants—within the four seas all are subjects and servants.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 臣父兄 and the 臣妾 formulation, which is the letter's point about ranking even kin as subjects.

decisions.reason: The note is only 〈衜音道。〉; the current English breaks the inner quotation and drops the closing annotation bracket.
宜登上公 names the highest ducal rank, not the office 太師; the next sentence makes him 太尉.

decisions.after: Sun Deng's birth mother had been a woman of humble station. Lady Xu had the grace of mothering him in his youth, but she was later cast aside for jealousy and sent to live in Wu, while Consort Lady Bu became Sun Quan's favorite.
decisions.reason: 少有母養之恩 means she mothered him in youth, not that she raised him only briefly; the proposed “had had” is awkward.
對曰：「在吳。」 is one quoted reply; the extra quote after answered is a punctuation error.
周晉、顏回 names Prince Jin of Zhou together with Yan Hui, not kings of Zhou and of Jin.
The same 周晉 is one person, Prince Jin of Zhou, not “the kings of Zhou and Jin.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 周晉、顏回有上智之才，而尚夭折

decisions.reason: 寬刑輕賦 means ease punishments and lighten levies, not widen punishments.
慮 is acceptably romanized Sun Lü (pinyin lǜ); replacing it with Sun Lu is spelling consistency, not a source error.
The same 慮 may be written Sun Lü; the change to Sun Lu is stylistic consistency, not a mistranslation of the Chinese.
慮弟也 is accurately “Lu’s younger brother”; adding the surname and choosing Lü is not required by the Chinese.
敦之子 is “the son of Dun”; the surname is already given for Zhang Chun in the same sentence, so the literal is accurate enough.
庶子 here is the heir’s household office, not a generic palace attendant.
寢疾 means he took to his sickbed, not a diagnosis of sleeping sickness.
上寢疾 is the same idiom of lying ill, not sleeping sickness.
謂尚、琮爲賢 names Shang and Cong, and 方之袁、劉 names Yuan and Liu; the current English omits both.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 袁紹、劉表謂尚、琮爲賢，本有傳後之意

decisions.reason: 殺申生 names Shen Sheng; “Crown Prince Sheng” drops 申.
猶生之年 means dying would still count as living; the current calque is unintelligible.
建業 is Jianye, the Wu capital’s contemporary name; Jiankang is a later name not in the Chinese.
吳興郡 is Wu Xing commandery, and 治烏程 is its administrative seat, not “Wu commandery of Xing.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 分吳郡、丹楊九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程

decisions.reason: 但遣使 uses the personal name 但 (Shi Dan), not the adverb “but only.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 但遣使以謙命詔丁固、諸葛靚

decisions.reason: 臨陣皆披散, after they were already 裸身無鎧甲, means they broke and scattered at the line, not that they wore their hair loose.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 但兵裸身無鎧甲，臨陣皆披散。

decisions.reason: Initial 但 is Dan’s name, and 披散 here is dispersal, not loosened hair.

decisions.reason: The sentence names 太伯順父之志 and the Han princes 河間獻王 and 東海王彊; collapsing them into unnamed “Han’s virtuous princes” omits the source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上惟太伯順父之志，中念河間獻王、東海王彊恭敬之節

decisions.reason: 臣父兄 and 四海之內，皆爲臣妾 are the point that even fathers and elder brothers rank as subjects; the current English omits that.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是以家天下，臣父兄，四海之內，皆爲臣妾。
